customer_question: Some of the newly-mandatory BAS/DIS/HIDS test items came back Fail or Indecisive. Is there any way around needing to pass them, short of fixing our firmware?
question_variants: Is there a workaround if our firmware can't pass the new mandatory BAS/DIS/HIDS items?
Can we reference someone else's existing registration for BAS/DIS/HIDS instead of testing our own firmware?
If our product doesn't actually use these profiles, do we still need to fix the firmware to pass them?
actual_issue: The customer's keyboard returned Fail or Indecisive results on some of the newly-mandatory BAS/DIS/HIDS minimum test items, and the customer was looking for a way to complete registration without modifying their firmware to genuinely pass those items.
plain_english_explanation: If a product can't pass tests for profiles it was only forced to add because of a recent rule change -- and the product never actually used those profiles' features to begin with -- there can be a shortcut: pointing the registration at an existing, already-passing registration for those specific profiles from a chipset or stack vendor, instead of fixing your own firmware to pass. This only makes sense if the product genuinely doesn't rely on those features, and it should be treated as a fallback, not the first thing to try.
consultant_answer: If the customer's existing model registered without BAS, DIS, or HIDS support has not experienced any market connectivity-compatibility problems, that is evidence the keyboard does not actually use BAS, DIS, or HIDS functionality. In that case, the registration can formally reference an existing Nordic Profile Subsystem registration (a specific QDID) that includes BAS 1.0, DIS 1.1, and HIDS, instead of preparing a firmware fix and obtaining a fresh Pass report for the items that returned Fail or Indecisive. This was explicitly framed as a last-resort 'escape route': the customer should first consider pursuing a firmware fix to genuinely pass the BAS/DIS/HIDS minimum items, with the Profile Subsystem reference workaround held in reserve only if that does not pan out.
decision_logic: Referencing an existing third-party Profile Subsystem registration to satisfy a newly-mandatory profile requirement is appropriate only when there is supporting evidence (such as a lack of market compatibility issues on a registration that lacked the profile) that the product does not actually rely on that profile's functionality, and should be pursued only after a genuine firmware fix has been considered, not as the default first response to a Fail/Indecisive result.
final_recommendation: Before recommending a third-party Profile Subsystem reference as a workaround for a Fail/Indecisive newly-mandatory profile item, check whether the product's existing registration (without that profile) has a track record free of market connectivity issues, and present the firmware-fix path as the primary recommendation, with the reference workaround offered only as a fallback.
risk_if_done_wrong: Defaulting to the third-party Profile Subsystem reference workaround without first confirming the product doesn't rely on the relevant profile's functionality risks registering a product that claims support for capabilities its actual firmware does not implement correctly.
